question: Why do we normally overlook the descend phase when calculating Point of Equal Time (PET)?

options.text: Because there are so many uncertain factors in the descend phase.
Because we never know what kind of descend clearance we will get from ATC.
Because the descend will have an equal effect, whatever destination we decide to proceed to.
Because the W/V during the descend is not known in academic situations.

explanation: The descent happens whichever way you go (continue or return), so it has the same effect on both legs and cancels out of the PET calculation.

question: Given: Distance A to B 1973 NM Groundspeed OUT 430 kt Groundspeed BACK 385 kt The time from A to the Point of Equal Time (PET) between A and B is:
explanation: Distance to PET = D × H / (O + H) = 1 973 × 385 / 815 ≈ 932 NM. Time = 932 / 430 ≈ 130 min.

question: Two points A and B are 1000 NM apart. TAS = 490 kt. On the flight between A and B the equivalent headwind is -20 kt. On the return leg between B and A, the equivalent headwind is +40 kt. What distance from A, along the route A to B, is the Point of Equal Time (PET)?
explanation: −20 headwind = 20 kt tailwind out: O = 510 kt; +40 headwind home: H = 450 kt. PET = D × H/(O + H) = 1 000 × 450 / 960 ≈ 470 NM.

question: An aircraft takes-off from an airport 2 hours before sunset. The pilot flies a track of 090° (T), W/V 130° / 20 kt, TAS 100 kt. In order to return to the point of departure before sunset, the furthest distance which may be travelled is:
explanation: Radius of action in 2 h: GS out ≈ 84 kt, GS home ≈ 114 kt. Distance = T × O × H / (O + H) = 2 × 84 × 114 / 198 ≈ 97 NM.

question: You have calculated Point of No Return (PNR) on a flight, having all negative WCs in the flight plan. During the flight you experience that the W/V is stronger but coming from the same direction as in the flight plan. Consider the following statements:

options.text: The PNR will not change because the neither TAS nor Fuel Flow has changed.
The PNR will, if recalculated, move toward the no-wind PNR.
You will arrive at the PNR at a later time than flight planned.
A recalculated PNR will move toward the place of departure.

explanation: Any wind reduces the PNR distance compared with still air; a stronger wind (same direction) moves the PNR further towards the departure point.

question: The distance from departure point to point of equal time is:

options.text: inversely proportional to groundspeed out and groundspeed back.

explanation: Distance to PET = D × H / (O + H): inversely proportional to the sum of the groundspeeds out and back.

question: For a distance of 1860 NM between Q and R, a ground speed OUT of 385 kt, a ground speed BACK of 465 kt and an endurance of 8 HR (excluding reserves) the distance from Q to the point of safe return (PSR) is:
explanation: PSR distance = E × O × H / (O + H) = 8 × 385 × 465 / 850 ≈ 1 685 NM.

question: Given: Distance Q to R 1760 NM Groundspeed out 435 kt Groundspeed back 385 kt Safe endurance 9 HR The distance from Q to the Point of Safe Return (PSR) between Q and R is:
explanation: PSR distance = E × O × H / (O + H) = 9 × 435 × 385 / 820 ≈ 1 838 NM.

question: Given: Distance A to B 2346 NM Groundspeed OUT 365 kt Groundspeed BACK 480 kt Safe endurance 8 HR 30 MIN The time from A to the Point of Safe Return (PSR) A is:
explanation: Time to PSR = E × H / (O + H) = 510 min × 480 / 845 ≈ 290 min.

question: Given: Distance A to B is 360 NM Wind component A - B is -15 kt Wind component B - A is +15 kt TAS is 180 kt. What is the distance from the equal-time-point to B?
explanation: O = 165 kt, H = 195 kt. PET from A = 360 × 195/360 = 195 NM, so from PET to B = 165 NM.

question: Flying from A to B, distance 3,016 nm, TAS 480 kts, there is a headwind of 90 kts and when flying from B to A there is a tailwind of 75 kts. If the aircraft leaves A at 1320 UTC what is the ETA at the equal time point?
An aeroplane is flying at TAS 180 kt on a track of 090° . The W/V is 045° / 50kt. How far can the aeroplane fly out from its base and return in one hour?
explanation: GS out ≈ 141 kt, GS home ≈ 212 kt. Radius = T × O × H/(O + H) = 1 × 141 × 212/353 ≈ 85 NM.

question: Given: Distance A to B 2484 NM Mean groundspeed out 420 kt Mean groundspeed back 500 kt Safe endurance 08 HR 30 MIN The distance from A to the Point of Safe Return (PSR) A is:

An aircraft was over A at 1435 hours flying direct to B. Given: Distance A to B 2900 NM True airspeed 470 kt Mean wind component OUT +55 kt Mean wind component BACK -75 kt Safe endurance 9 HR 30 MIN The distance from A to the Point of Safe Return (PSR) A is:

You fly from C to D, a distance of 450 NM. The WC C - D is +30, and the WC D - C is -40. TAS is 160 Kt and reduced TAS is 130 Kt. The Fuel Flow is 165 kg/hr, and the Safe endurance when overhead C is 4 hours. Calculate PET between C and D, based on reduced TAS for the flight from PET to C/D. What is the flying time from C to PET?
explanation: With reduced TAS from the PET: O = 130 + 30 = 160 kt, H = 130 − 40 = 90 kt. PET = 450 × 90/250 = 162 NM. Flown at normal TAS (GS 190 kt): 162/190 h ≈ 0:51.

question: An aircraft was over Q at 1320 hours flying direct to R. Given: Distance Q to R 3016 NM True airspeed 480 kt Mean wind component out 90 kt Mean wind component back 75 kt Safe endurance 10:00 HR The distance from Q to the Point of Safe Return (PSR) Q is:

You fly from C to D, a distance of 450 NM. The WC C - D is +30, and the WC D - C is -40. TAS is 160 Kt and reduced TAS is 130 Kt. The Fuel Flow is 165 kg/hr, and the Safe endurance when overhead C is 4 hours. Calculate PNR for return to C. What is the distance from PNR to D?
explanation: PNR on normal TAS: O = 190 kt, H = 120 kt. Time = 4 × 120/310 ≈ 1.55 h → 294 NM from C, i.e. ≈ 156 NM short of D.

question: Under which circumstances will an aircrafts radius of action be greatest?
explanation: Any wind reduces radius of action; an along-track wind reduces it more than a pure crosswind, so a direct crosswind gives the greatest radius.

question: The distance from A to B is 2368 nautical miles. If outbound groundspeed in 365 knots and homebound groundspeed is 480 knots and safe endurance is 8 hours 30 minutes, what is the time to the PNR?
explanation: Time to PNR = E × H/(O + H) = 510 × 480/845 ≈ 290 min.

question: An aircraft was over Q at 1320 hours flying direct to R. Given: Distance Q to R 3016 NM True airspeed 480 kt Mean wind component OUT -90 kt Mean wind component BACK +75 kt. The ETA for reaching the Point of Equal Time (PET) between Q and R is:

An aircraft has a TAS of 300 knots and is over a stretch of water between 2 airfields 500 nm apart. If the wind component is 60 knots head, what is the distance from the first airfield to the critical point?
explanation: O = 240 kt, H = 360 kt. CP = 500 × 360/600 = 300 NM from the first airfield.

question: An aircraft has a TAS of 300 knots and a safe endurance of 10 hours. If the wind component on the outbound leg is 50 knots head, what is the distance to the point of safe endurance?
The Point of No Return (PNR) is a function of:
explanation: PNR depends on the safe endurance (usable fuel) and the groundspeeds out and home: T = E × H/(O + H). It does not depend on the distance between departure and destination.

question: Distance Q to R 1 970 NM, groundspeed out 495 kt, groundspeed back 465 kt, safe endurance 9 h. The distance from Q to the Point of Safe Return is:
explanation: PSR distance = E × O × H/(O + H) = 9 × 495 × 465/960 ≈ 2 158 NM.

question: The effect on the position of the Critical Point (CP) of reducing the TAS when there is a headwind component outbound will be to:
explanation: CP = D × H/(O + H). A wind moves the CP into wind (further out with a headwind outbound). Lower TAS makes the wind relatively stronger, so the CP moves further from departure.

question: Route A–B 345 NM (WC +35), B–C 320 NM (WC +15), C–D 440 NM (WC −30). TAS 350 kt on 4 engines, fuel flow 5 200 kg/h. Fuel at take-off 30 000 kg, of which 4 000 kg must remain on return to A. The time to the PNR is approximately:
explanation: Usable 26 000 kg. A–B out + back uses 10 354 kg, B–C 9 526 kg → 6 120 kg left at C. On C–D each NM out-and-back costs 16.25 + 13.68 kg → ≈ 205 NM beyond C. Time = 53.8 + 52.6 + 38.3 ≈ 145 min ≈ 147.

question: Same route (A–B 345 NM WC +35, B–C 320 NM WC +15, C–D 440 NM WC −30). TAS on 3 engines 300 kt. Find the distance from A to the critical point, assuming an engine fails at the CP:
explanation: With 3-engine GS (out 335/315/270, back 265/285/330), equating time onward to D with time back to A gives the CP ≈ 546 NM from A (in the B–C leg).
